{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01AzE42b1VP9MfujZEMmknjj","type":"tool_result","content":"# predictable-code-claude

The [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com) plugin for **Predictable Code** —
spec-driven formal verification in the loop. It turns any project you open into a
closed verification loop: you edit code, Predictable re-translates / analyzes /
verifies it against its spec, and lifecycle hooks feed the verdict back to the
agent.

The plugin exposes **exactly one command — `predictable sync`** — which runs the
whole pipeline internally (translate → analyze → infer → prove/verify →
diagnose) and returns a single verdict. No other verbs, no MCP server, and
**zero configuration**.

> This repo contains **no Predictable source code** — only the plugin
> (manifest, hooks, scripts, one skill). It runs the `predictable` CLI you
> install (below), or a compiled runtime it downloads from a token-gated,
> artifacts-only distribution repository. The Predictable source stays private.

## Install

### 1. The `predictable` CLI

Install it with the command the hosted Control Center shows under
**Settings › Connected machines**:

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://<control-center>/i/<code>/predictable-install.sh && bash predictable-install.sh
```

It installs Predictable Code and puts `predictable` on your `PATH` (open a new
shell, and start Claude Code from it, so the session sees it). With no runtime
bundle of its own, the plugin runs that `predictable` — `bin/predictable` falls
back to the one on `PATH` — so nothing else is needed.

**Alternative: the runtime bundle.** With a distribution token set, the
`SessionStart` hook downloads the per-platform runtime bundle (the `predictable`
CLI + `predictable_java_direct` + pinned `z3` + relocatable Lean toolchain +
prebuilt `.lake` oleans) into the plugin's data directory on the first session,
and uses it instead:

```sh
export PREDICTABLE_DIST_TOKEN=<your-token>
```

The token unlocks only the compiled runtime — it grants no access to any source.
With neither, the plugin degrades gracefully (a `systemMessage`, never a broken
session).

### 2. The plugin, in the repositories that should be analysed

Add the marketplace once:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add predictable-machines/predictable-code-claude
```

then, from the root of each repository that should be analysed:

```sh
claude plugin install predictable-code@predictable-machines --scope local
```

**Choose the scope.** `claude plugin install` defaults to **user** scope, which
turns the plugin on in **every** repository you open with Claude Code — and its
hooks initialise Predictable Code there, sync it, and **publish** each analysis
(a push to origin's `predictable-code-database` branch). Install it per
repository instead:

| Scope | Recorded in | Who gets it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `--scope local` (recommended for yourself) | `.claude/settings.local.json`, not committed | you, in this repository |
| `--scope project` (recommended for a team) | `.claude/settings.json`, committed | everyone who opens this repository with Claude Code |
| `--scope user` (the default) | `~/.claude/settings.json` | you, in every repository |

For `--scope project`, declare the marketplace in the repository too
(`claude plugin marketplace add predictable-machines/predictable-code-claude --scope project`),
so a teammate's Claude Code can find the plugin it names.

Already installed at user scope? Remove it there
(`claude plugin uninstall predictable-code@predictable-machines --scope user`)

	@echo ""
	@echo "No-key / no-bundle (run on every PR):"

	@echo "  make test-plugin-mcp      L3: 'predictable sync --json' contract on a clone"

	@shellcheck -x scripts/*.sh tests/*.sh bin/predictable

test-plugin: test-plugin-validate test-plugin-hooks
	@echo "test-plugin: L1 + L2 passed"

# L4 — configuration self-check. Reports which pieces are present; needs the
# runtime bundle installed (SessionStart bootstrap, PREDICTABLE_DIST_TOKEN).

	@bash scripts/doctor.sh

# L3 — 'predictable sync --json' contract against a real clone. Requires the
# runtime bundle. Point PROJECT at a checkout of predictable-code-java-reference.
PROJECT ?= .
test-plugin-mcp:
	@echo "L3: running 'predictable sync --json' in $(PROJECT)"
	@if [ ! -x bin/predictable ]; then echo "bin/predictable not executable"; exit 1; fi
	@cd "$(PROJECT)" && CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT="$(CURDIR)" "$(CURDIR)/bin/predictable" sync --json | jq -e 'keys[0]' >/dev/null \
		&& echo "L3: sync produced a well-formed SyncResponse"

# L5 — headless end-to-end. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + the runtime bundle.

	@if [ -z "$$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then echo "test-plugin-e2e-claude: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY required — skipping"; exit 0; fi

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # L1 + L2: fast, key-free, bundle-free, source-free. Runs on every PR.
  plugin:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install shellcheck + jq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y shellcheck jq

      - name: Lint (shellcheck)
        run: make lint

      - name: L2 — validate plugin surface + privacy
        run: make test-plugin-validate

      - name: L1 — hook contract tests
        run: make test-plugin-hooks

  # Privacy guard: fail the build if any Predictable source ever lands here.
  no-source-leak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Assert no Predictable source is tracked
        run: |
          leak=$(git ls-files | grep -E '\.lean$|(^|/)lakefile|(^|/)packages/' || true)
          if [ -n "$leak" ]; then
            echo "::error::Predictable source leaked into the plugin repo:"
            echo "$leak"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "No source-like files tracked."

The [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com) plugin for **Predictable Code** —
spec-driven formal verification in the loop. It turns any project you open into a
closed verification loop: you edit code, Predictable re-translates / analyzes /
verifies it against its spec, and lifecycle hooks feed the verdict back to the
agent.

The plugin exposes **exactly one command — `predictable sync`** — which runs the
whole pipeline internally (translate → analyze → infer → prove/verify →
diagnose) and returns a single verdict. No other verbs, no MCP server, and
**zero configuration**.

> This repo contains **no Predictable source code** — only the plugin
> (manifest, hooks, scripts, one skill). It runs the `predictable` CLI you
> install (below), or a compiled runtime it downloads from a token-gated,
> artifacts-only distribution repository. The Predictable source stays private.

## Install

### 1. The `predictable` CLI

Install it with the command the hosted Control Center shows under
**Settings › Connected machines**:

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://<control-center>/i/<code>/predictable-install.sh && bash predictable-install.sh
```

It installs Predictable Code and puts `predictable` on your `PATH` (open a new
shell, and start Claude Code from it, so the session sees it). With no runtime
bundle of its own, the plugin runs that `predictable` — `bin/predictable` falls
back to the one on `PATH` — so nothing else is needed.

**Alternative: the runtime bundle.** With a distribution token set, the
`SessionStart` hook downloads the per-platform runtime bundle (the `predictable`
CLI + `predictable_java_direct` + pinned `z3` + relocatable Lean toolchain +
prebuilt `.lake` oleans) into the plugin's data directory on the first session,
and uses it instead:

```sh
export PREDICTABLE_DIST_TOKEN=<your-token>
```

The token unlocks only the compiled runtime — it grants no access to any source.
With neither, the plugin degrades gracefully (a `systemMessage`, never a broken
session).

### 2. The plugin, in the repositories that should be analysed

Add the marketplace once:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add predictable-machines/predictable-code-claude
```

then, from the root of each repository that should be analysed:

```sh
claude plugin install predictable-code@predictable-machines --scope local
```

**Choose the scope.** `claude plugin install` defaults to **user** scope, which
turns the plugin on in **every** repository you open with Claude Code — and its
hooks initialise Predictable Code there, sync it, and **publish** each analysis
(a push to origin's `predictable-code-database` branch). Install it per
repository instead:

| Scope | Recorded in | Who gets it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `--scope local` (recommended for yourself) | `.claude/settings.local.json`, not committed | you, in this repository |
| `--scope project` (recommended for a team) | `.claude/settings.json`, committed | everyone who opens this repository with Claude Code |
| `--scope user` (the default) | `~/.claude/settings.json` | you, in every repository |

For `--scope project`, declare the marketplace in the repository too
(`claude plugin marketplace add predictable-machines/predictable-code-claude --scope project`),
so a teammate's Claude Code can find the plugin it names.

Already installed at user scope? Remove it there
(`claude plugin uninstall predictable-code@predictable-machines --scope user`)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L2 plugin validation (no LLM, no bundle): every JSON parses, the manifest
# declares exactly the intended surface (one skill, the report command, hooks, NO
# userConfig, NO MCP server), and — privacy-critical — the repo carries NO
# Predictable source.
set -u

ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)
fail=0
ok() { printf '  ok   — %s\n' "$1"; }
bad() {
  printf '  FAIL — %s\n' "$1"
  fail=$((fail + 1))
}
# judge <exit-status> <ok-msg> <fail-msg>
judge() {
  if [ "$1" -eq 0 ]; then ok "$2"; else bad "$3"; fi
}

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "validate: jq is required"
  exit 1
}

echo "== JSON well-formedness =="
while IFS= read -r f; do
  jq -e . "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1
  judge $? "parses: ${f#"$ROOT"/}" "invalid JSON: ${f#"$ROOT"/}"
done < <(find "$ROOT" -name '*.json' -not -path '*/.git/*')

echo "== plugin.json surface =="
P="$ROOT/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
jq -e '.name == "predictable-code"' "$P" >/dev/null 2>&1
judge $? "name is predictable-code" "plugin name wrong/missing"
jq -e '.description | length > 0' "$P" >/dev/null 2>&1
judge $? "has description" "description missing"
jq -e 'has("userConfig") | not' "$P" >/dev/null 2>&1
judge $? "no userConfig (zero configuration)" "userConfig present — must be absent"
jq -e 'has("mcpServers") | not' "$P" >/dev/null 2>&1
judge $? "no mcpServers (MCP not shipped)" "mcpServers present — must be absent"

ok() { printf '  ok   — %s\n' "$1"; }
bad() {
  printf '  FAIL — %s\n' "$1"
  fail=$((fail + 1))

# judge <exit-status> <ok-msg> <fail-msg>
judge() {
  if [ "$1" -eq 0 ]; then ok "$2"; else bad "$3"; fi

  echo "validate: jq is required"
